I am 70 this year, and I have farmed all my life, so I do not want to spread myself too thin. My family has seven people, but some work off-farm, so I will keep the work simple and steady. Since cotton is still my main cropping system, I will put the largest share of land into cotton, but I will also keep some wheat and maize for income balance and to avoid putting everything into one crop. I have well irrigation, so I can protect the crops at key times, but I will not chase very high input because I am more concerned with stable harvests than taking big risks.

For wheat, I will keep a moderate area and manage it in the usual local way with improved seed, enough fertilizer, and a few irrigations because wheat here responds well to water at the right stages. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because it is more dependable for yield, and I will keep fertilizer balanced so the plants stand strong in summer. For cotton, I will still plant the largest area because that is the crop I know best, but I will control inputs and labor by using improved seed, rotary tillage, and a moderate number of sprays and irrigations. I will not make the plan too aggressive, because at my age I prefer a plan I know I can carry through properly.
